target: Feature parity is the requested target. Approved V1 scope reductions (2026-11-27): no real-application pilot, no qualification by outside people (screen-reader, physical IME or device testers, independent collaborators), and no independent-writer or independent-consumer release requirements.

features.summary: Paragraph and heading editing
features.current: Rust rich actions and the shared editor support paragraphs, ranked headings, split/join and retained identity.
features.acceptance: Keep all six heading ranks, text formatting, local/shared history and recovery consistent in one installed V1 editor.

features.summary: Bold, italic, underline, strike and inline code
features.current: The explicit standard profile has local/shared stock controls driven by Rust exact/mixed state, including marks, caret overrides, keyboard submission and one-group formatting history. Tests cover clipboard, exact reload, offline merge and selective Undo. Released ABI 3 Highlight checkpoints now reopen with full Undo/Redo in the current reader, and HTML import resolves supported text-decoration shorthand through the native style cascade. Promotion into the default distributed profile and the remaining integrated V1 workflows (including the catalog clear-formatting and highlight cases) are still open.
features.acceptance: Ship all everyday marks in the combined profile, renderer and toolbar; test mixed state, caret formats, clipboard, offline edits and selective Undo/Redo.

features.summary: Subscript and superscript
features.current: The experimental standard profile now has explicit script-switching controls in local/shared editors, with one Undo group and exact recovered history in cells/captions. The model still admits independent literals and never silently normalizes them. V1 promotion and complete foreign interchange remain open.
features.acceptance: Define mutually compatible script formats, semantic presentation and exact history/interchange behavior.

features.summary: Font family, size, text and background color
features.current: The standard profile has local/shared mixed-value forms and reset controls for RGB24 text/background colors, integer 8..96 pixel sizes and four font-family presets. Empty resets preserve exact history and Redo. HTML import now converts the CSS font shorthand with the same bounded family, size, weight, style and line-height rules as longhands, honours shorthand resets, !important and parent inheritance, and matches bounded tag/class/ID stylesheet selectors (up to three descendant parts). System font keywords and unsupported components produce loss notices. Arbitrary CSS and embedded fonts are unsupported; promotion into the default distributed profile and broader producer interchange remain open.
features.acceptance: Promote safe declarative presentations into the combined editor, define supported font/size/color domains and test interoperability.

features.summary: Links and automatic link detection
features.current: Default and explicit standard rich/shared Link forms reuse the same safe URL policy. Standard forms support mixed values, stale guards and exact history/reload. Explicit native property patches preserve each observed URL or target when the other form field is left blank; every selected character must already carry a Link. Complete set commands retain replacement semantics. Shared patches use original complete-format annotations and whole-format concurrent conflict policy. Opt-in autolink-v1 converts a typed http(s)/www URL on space or Enter into the standard link only when the target is already canonical under the native safeLinkV1 subset; trailing punctuation stays plain and one Undo removes only the link. Input rules, including autolink, now run in a focused candidate profile against fresh SDK archives, and pinned earlier local readers restore input-rule checkpoints exactly. Broader foreign interchange and release qualification remain open.
features.acceptance: Use one safe URL policy for shared rendering, explicit link editing, clipboard/export and optional autolink, without interpreting arbitrary HTML.

features.summary: Blockquotes, code blocks and horizontal rules
features.current: Explicit local/shared structural V2 provides quote, code and rule commands, safe rendering, code-language controls, same-block replacement and guarded code exit. Installed vanilla/React, reference relay, explicit/natural history and rich interchange paths exist; creator Undo retains peer text for later Redo/recovery. Shared code-block history now recovers exactly after reload, and a journal captured from the first shared structural V2 SDK reopens byte-for-byte with both history branches in native and installed Wasm readers. This is a functional candidate, not a frozen V1 grammar or completed physical-input, producer-fidelity and release qualification.
features.acceptance: Add original Rust contracts and separate actions for each kind, including code language/text rules, boundary navigation, shared conflict policy and migration.

features.summary: Hard breaks and navigation around atomic blocks
features.current:
Local/shared native hard breaks retain one LF, and logical navigation preserves atom stops, transparent containers, cell/caption domains, ranges, read-only policy and Redo. Separate commands create text beside atoms or delete/replace whole images, visible tables and rules; installed typing beside an atom now stays inside the native Undo window in candidate CI. Rust chooses directional recovery and fresh floors for sole-child/hidden-only parent remainders; plain/first-key replacement retains exact original-family history and peer causal text. Typing after a line break at the end of a text block lands after it in Chromium and WebKit through a presentation-only trailing
. Hard breaks now survive Word export and HTML import outside the Apple clipboard newline marker. Missing first-key beforeinput and uncancelled paging defaults have reproduced controller repairs. Shared replacement needs transient insertion headroom. Physical/bidi arrows, gap/drop positions, general ranges, already hidden-only documents, native OS atom clipboard/input and final reliability qualification remain incomplete.
features.acceptance: Specify soft-break semantics, create reachable text positions around every atom, and test Shift+Enter, arrows, deletion and empty-document recovery.

features.summary: Bullet and numbered nested lists
features.current: Rich and shared paths implement indentation, outdentation, item split/join and list conversion with retained content.
features.acceptance: Retain the same list contract in the V1 installable profile and native/browser mixed-content tests.

features.summary: Interactive task lists
features.current: Explicit local/shared structural V2 provides typed completion, pointer/Space checkboxes, item split/join, nesting, conversion and empty exit. General and document selections, Rust-admitted rich clipboard and the optional foreign adapter now reach the installed mixed workflow. Offline completion versus nesting, selective history and exact recovery are covered by focused native/SDK/relay tests. Public V1 promotion, broader producer fidelity and physical-input/reliability qualification remain open.
features.acceptance: Add typed checked state with keyboard and pointer behavior, nesting, clipboard, conflict policy and author-local history.

features.summary: List numbering and marker properties
features.current: Positive ordered-list starts are supported. Rich language V4 (released, frozen) adds five ordered numbering styles (decimal, lower/upper alpha, lower/upper roman) and HTML-compatible reversed counting, as one history group, locally and in shared V4 (`set_list_numbering`, with a start change in the same Undo group; a split list's tail keeps its style and counting order), with local and shared toolbar controls and identical HTML/Markdown/DOCX interchange and Office paste. DOCX export now keeps descending decimal markers for reversed lists within a documented range, and HTML import keeps Word flat-list numbering hints. An opt-in presentation-only legal multi-level numbering mode (`legalListNumbering`) derives 1.1.1 markers (docs/LIST_STRUCTURE.md). Missing: bullet marker styles, decimal-leading-zero and other counter styles, stored legal multi-level numbering (needs a new language version) and per-item overrides.
features.acceptance: Define each numbering/style domain, restart/continuation behavior and deterministic nested export, cover bullet styles and legal multi-level numbering or record them as approved exclusions, and release V4, before claiming advanced list parity.

features.summary: Alignment, block indent, direction and line height controls
features.current: Explicit layout V3 provides bounded native alignment, indent, direction and line-height fields, independent shared updates, safe rendering and mixed/inherited vanilla/React controls. The optional interchange adapter carries representable layout with explicit HTML fallback/loss notices, and now honours authored alignment inside legacy email center wrappers. A journal captured from the first shared layout SDK reopens byte-for-byte in the installed shared reader with its future Undo/Redo checkpoints. Installed mixed editing and focused offline/recovery matrices exercise this candidate; complete bidi editing, broader producer fidelity and V1 qualification remain unfinished.
features.acceptance: Add bounded semantic block properties, direction-aware selection/layout and safe rendering/interchange, not arbitrary stored CSS.

features.summary: Text, node, grid and document-wide editing selections
features.current: Explicit general and document scopes now cover partial table/image preservation, rich Copy with empty unselected cells, atomic deletion/replacement, Enter/composition and whole-document Select All without manufacturing text endpoints. Caption/code flow/grid paste uses the approved text-with-loss notice policy. Installed mixed workflows combine both history policies, foreign paste, offline authors, fresh IDs, exact recovery and peer-preserving Undo/Redo through writer transport V2. Original defaults and saved families remain distinct. Physical input, supported-environment reliability, public API/migration and final V1 qualification remain open.
features.acceptance: Specify and implement document-wide Select All, deletion, replacement and formatting across lists, tables, captions and atoms in both directions.

features.summary: Undo, Redo and natural typing groups
features.current: Exact local/selective shared history and compound formatting are implemented. Native local and shared typing reach opt-in Wasm, vanilla/React, durable sessions and DOM boundaries. Separate declared families preserve exact grouped recovery; older runtimes reject unsupported modes. Atomic legacy upgrades retain Redo, failed saves retain recovery, and invisible Undo publications autosave. Slash commands run as one native replaceTriggerThen history group, including in shared batches. Installed Chrome records now show pre-cut Undo/Redo and offline frames surviving two journal seals, exact portable history restore into fresh databases, and pinned historical checkpoints (V0.1.0, ABI 3 Highlight, ABI 4 typed range) replaying full history. Measured installed Chrome cost grows with history: over 100 two-peer edit/Undo rounds typing rose from about 40 to 219 ms and Undo from 41 to 229 ms, and one run's native journal refused synchronization after round 109. Recorded Firefox method calls can still exceed the 750ms group gap; older WebKit startup, replay/cancel and offline-button observations remain open. The shared replay journal stays bounded at 1,000 entries and 16 MiB, which is not a rolling 1,000-action Undo window. Supported history sizes and client/relay lifecycle rotation are unresolved V1 work.
features.acceptance: Define typing/paste/composition/format/move grouping, preserve remote work under local Undo, and test future Redo after recovery.

features.summary: Breditor structural clipboard
features.current: The original rich clipboard now also reaches general/document selections, preserving partially selected structures and empty unselected table cells. Guarded Copy/Cut/Paste uses Rust admission with fresh identities, one history group and exact recovery in local/shared owners. Optional foreign formats are supplied by the separate interchange adapter; native clipboard and final release qualification remain distinct.
features.acceptance: Keep exact source preservation, one-step cut/paste history and cross-peer clipboard behavior in the installed V1 editor.

features.summary: Sanitized HTML import and semantic export
features.current: The opt-in @breditor/interchange adapter imports inert bounded HTML and emits allowlisted semantic HTML through Rust clipboard admission. Local/shared managed and React openings provide explicit priority, stale guards, four-format retention, host-owned image mapping and post-publication loss notices. Import now matches bounded tag/class/ID stylesheet selectors, resolves font shorthand, honors CSS dimensions over HTML size hints, keeps declared column-group and cell widths, admits sibling figure captions on tables, rejects nested tables in captions and preserves authored breaks outside the Apple clipboard sentinel. Export keeps captions below the grid and disclosure-summary whitespace. Explicit full-page HTML import/export with bounded metadata, portable HTML with verified host-owned rasters, and revision-fenced Base64 HTML paste are separate opt-in entry points. The installed source API and optional peer boundary are checked from clean installs. Arbitrary HTML/CSS, captured-producer fidelity and physical clipboard/final release qualification remain open.
features.acceptance: Build separate import/export adapters with declared loss diagnostics, resource bounds, URL policy, asset references and rich round-trip fixtures.

features.summary: Markdown import, export and paste
features.current: The separate optional adapter implements a named version-one CommonMark-based dialect with tables, strikethrough, task markers and sanitized raw HTML. It imports/exports through native schema validation and advertises Markdown MIME explicitly. Safe HTML fallback and compatibility/loss notices cover unrepresentable layout, rich tables, captions and exact code. Export alternates list markers so adjacent lists stay separate, emits hard breaks, GFM column alignment, empty fences and safe images, and reports dropped fence info and raw HTML comments as losses; ordered starts below 1 become 1 with a list-numbering notice. Import optionally links GFM autolink literals (autolinks: true) under the same grammar as typed autolink-v1. Hosts can now call dom.pasteText(text, "detect-markdown") as an explicit action: it converts only an ATX heading, a blank line and at least two flat, consistently marked bullet items, as one Undo step; other text stays literal. Ordinary text/plain clipboard events are never guessed as Markdown. Missing: automatic detection on ordinary plain-text paste beyond that narrow explicit pattern, full GFM conformance and release qualification.
features.acceptance: Qualify the versioned Markdown dialect and automatic detection on plain-text paste. Preserve representable semantics, report losses and test round trips.

features.summary: Word, Google Docs and spreadsheet rich paste
features.current: Representative Word/Docs/Excel markup fixtures exercise bounded stylesheet/list/table/merge conversion, formatting, links and host-owned images through the same Rust admission and paste actions. Combined installed offline/history/restart workflows cover those fixtures and explicit destination losses. A reconstructed producer corpus (Word desktop/web, Google Docs/Sheets, Excel, LibreOffice, Cocoa) drives exact structure/loss tests; nested Docs/Cocoa lists, Word lettered/roman/skipped levels, Word web list rebuilding, Docs script marks and file: image losses are handled. Word desktop and web lettered/roman numbering maps to V4 list styles where the owner supports list numbering, and HTML numbering hints in Word flat lists are now kept. Authored line breaks outside the Apple clipboard sentinel are preserved. These are authored or reconstructed snippets, not captured application-native clipboard dumps; real captured producer fixtures, broader fidelity and release qualification remain required.
features.acceptance: Maintain real producer fixtures and sanitization/loss policies; test lists, styles, tables, links and images through the same Rust admission boundary.

features.summary: Table geometry, cell bodies and grid operations
features.current: Creation/removal, row/column edits/moves, headers, merge/split, width values, rich cells and grid navigation/clipboard are functionally tested.
features.acceptance: Preserve the complete command set, rich content and selective history under the production package and all supported engines.

features.summary: Table presentation and advanced interaction
features.current: Width and header controls exist, plus opt-in accessible column-resize separators (one width command per drag or key, clamped to 32..4096). Local and shared editors can opt into keyboard-scrollable table viewports with localized labels, touch-sized controls and direction-aware edge states that retain position across redraws. Rich language V4 adds an optional trailing table caption with add/remove commands and table-action, navigation, clipboard, search and HTML interchange, locally and in shared V4 (`add_table_caption`/`remove_table_caption`, one Undo step; a second concurrent caption stays hidden). HTML import now admits a sibling figcaption on a native table, keeps authored cell widths under widthless columns and column groups, and rejects nested tables inside captions; export writes the caption first with caption-side:bottom so it renders below the grid. Missing: table and cell styling (borders, backgrounds, padding, cell alignment), configurable caption placement, layout tables and nested tables. The current grammar rejects nested tables; V1 includes them.
features.acceptance: Qualify nested-table editing, navigation, history and interchange alongside captions, accessible resize handles, table and cell presentation, and rich paste with intact source partitions.

features.summary: Block raster images and durable assets
features.current: PNG/JPEG/WebP admission, paste/drop, alt/decorative, captions, dimensions, replacement/removal, offline uploads and cross-host bytes are implemented. Explicit whole-store raster archives retain exact bytes, queue states and cancellation epochs, with canonical framing and atomic restore into an exact empty destination. An archive captured from the first Raster Asset Archive V1 source restores and re-exports through the installed browser reader. Corrupt retained duplicates are refused before admission, and admitted bytes stay independent of a later change to the selected file. The reference relay can run raster admission in a supervised worker process with Unix resource ceilings. Archives are not automatically coordinated with native sessions, outboxes or server state.
features.acceptance: Preserve byte-first durability, binding epochs, cancelled uploads and independent document/asset save indicators in the V1 package.

features.summary: Image layouts, handles, links and external sources
features.current: Numeric dimensions and block captions work. Opt-in accessible resize handles (aspect-keeping corner, edges, keyboard, RTL-aware) exist for local and shared editors; oversized images now start from a proportionally fitted size. Rich language V4 adds image links (canonical http(s) targets, optional new window, inert while editing), locally and in shared V4. New explicit host APIs: prepareRichRasterUrl checks an allowlisted HTTPS URL and verifies bytes returned by a host-owned loader against a pinned SHA-256 record; prepareRichRasterRendition picks a pinned narrower rendition or falls back to the verified original; @breditor/interchange/portable-html embeds host-owned rasters as data URLs; and portable-html-import admits bounded canonical Base64 PNG/JPEG/WebP data URLs for revision-fenced whole-document paste. Missing: an insert-by-URL editor action and implicit remote-load policy, inline and wrapped image styles, responsive srcset output, the CKBox/CKFinder/Uploadcare integrations, an optimization provider and the configured upload adapters.
features.acceptance: Qualify image layouts and responsive output, both URL insertion and policy-controlled implicit loading, Base64 uploads, the three asset provider integrations, optimization and asset lifecycle.

features.summary: Simultaneous rich editing and selective history
features.current: Rust replicas and the reference relay integrate concurrent text, list, table and image edits while retaining author-local Undo/Redo.
features.acceptance: Keep the native contracts and mixed browser workflow passing against the final released artifacts.

features.summary: Offline editing, reconnect and exact reload
features.current: Exclusive writer ownership, durable local journals, queued uploads, reconnect and exact reload work through browser and network tests. Independently verified archives preserve document, review and raster data through non-overwriting recovery, including after a live IndexedDB upgrade. Native server-log and independent document and comment history generations preserve offline work and future Undo/Redo. Installed Chrome records show pre-cut Undo/Redo and offline frames surviving two journal seals and exact portable restore into fresh databases. Relay tests recover acknowledged edits, comments and an upload after forced process exit before a new snapshot. Portable predecessor compaction retires raw archives and redundant checkpoints while preserving the selected terminal cut, offline work and Undo/Redo. Supported history and document lifetime limits are not defined (one installed run refused journal synchronization after 109 edit/Undo rounds), and final durability qualification remains open.
features.acceptance: Qualify supported history/document limits and operational recovery, not only the normal offline/reconnect path.

features.summary: Authenticated peer carets and selections
features.current: Lease-bound ephemeral presence resolves causal text/node/grid anchors and paints a separate read-only overlay, which the first-party pilot also shows. The overlay is aria-hidden and has no accessible equivalent. Placement and accessibility have not been qualified across supported layouts (mixed-direction text, scroll containers, touch).
features.acceptance: Retain expiry, fencing and read-only behavior; qualify overlay placement and accessibility in the supported layouts.

features.summary: Permissions and application authentication
features.current: Reference-room Reader/Editor authority and revocation are enforced. Explicit native routers can additionally use a separate durable serving epoch with real process-level locks; every native transaction and private capture rechecks it. The relay bounds document-server and upload request bodies before reading them. The first-party pilot issues per-participant codes and isolates journals and images by authenticated workspace. The Unix reference backend requires one protected non-rollback authority namespace and does not complete client/provider reconciliation or authenticated recovery activation. There are no host identity adapters, member/permission views, tenant provisioning or TLS deployment.
features.acceptance: Provide host identity adapters, room lifecycle, secure credential storage, observable denial/revocation and deployment guidance with independent authorization tests.

features.summary: Native live read-only editing
features.current: Both rich languages have native local/shared host policy, initial SDK options and live vanilla/React setters. It rejects authoring, pending styles and history while retaining selection, copy, incoming updates and durability. Surface/captions, task widgets, toolbar, keyboard, beforeinput, Cut-as-Copy, composition queues and asynchronous assets share the policy. Lock/unlock fences old intents without a history entry. Policy is not stored permission: restored owners start editable and hosts reapply it. Installed three-engine and real-relay tests pass; editable-region restrictions are tracked separately.
features.acceptance: Enforce read-only consistently for keyboard, beforeinput, clipboard, API, toolbar, composition and remote updates; define editable-region restrictions separately.

features.summary: Editable region restrictions
features.current: Native block-region restricted editing (docs/RESTRICTED_EDITING.md): a live host policy outside the frozen V4 grammar names editable subtrees by retained block ids. Rust admits every local command, mixed request, native command group, pending style and Undo/Redo by its complete effect, and anything that would change protected content is refused whole (`breditor_rich.restricted`). Cross-region selections are refused, not clamped; leaf regions refuse Enter and boundary merges while container regions allow new blocks; Undo of protected history is refused. Local Wasm, DOM and SDK provide `restrictedEditing:{policy}`, Tab/Shift+Tab region navigation, presentation-only region marking and Rust-derived toolbar disabling, qualified in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. Shared owners enforce the same rule natively for local work while incoming peer changes stay unfiltered; the policy is a host input, never persisted. Missing: inline exceptions (a V5 grammar change), shared DOM/SDK wiring, and relay or server enforcement.
features.acceptance: Define and enforce protected/editable identities through cross-region selections, moves, atomic mixed requests, pending styles, history authorization and remote changes; qualify persistence and host/server authority separately.

features.summary: Composable feature and custom-node SDK
features.current: Typed inline declarations, profile fingerprints and custom toolbar callbacks exist. The typed inline seam carries a first-party extension end to end (ruby: manifest, own fingerprint, generic commands and history, shared merging, closed presentation, interchange and toolbar controls). Shared structural grammar is sealed; arbitrary custom blocks/node views, extension dependencies, failure isolation and a conformance suite are not a supported extension SDK.
features.acceptance: Stabilize Breditor-owned schema/action/render/converter capabilities, dependencies, failure isolation and conformance tests without adopting another editor's protocol.

features.summary: Expandable toolbars, context menus and selection UI
features.current: Local/shared standard controls share field widgets and Rust-derived state, keyboard actions, editor focus return and stale-draft rejection. Owner-bound controls reject another editor before host mutation; custom owner-neutral controls remain reusable. Default compiled action-state APIs remain distinct. Opt-in floating selection toolbars and keyboard-reachable context menus borrow admitted controls through the same widget, Rust-derived state, gating, command path and focus return for local and shared editors. The same borrowed-control contract drives an opt-in menu bar, empty-line block menu and balloon-block preset (editor-shell-and-help). Borrowed form panels inside menus are now reachable with Tab, with the Tab exception scoped to owned form panels. These surfaces are covered in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit for focus, keyboard and shared Rust-derived state. Missing: grouped toolbar overflow, dropdown action groups, explicit row breaks and screen-reader qualification.
features.acceptance: One command/state contract must drive buttons, keyboard, forms and context menus with active/mixed/disabled state and consistent focus return.

features.summary: Find and replace
features.current: The optional Rust rich core has source-bound Unicode literal/regex search, semantic table/caption traversal and atomic local/shared Replace One/All. Opaque Wasm/SDK results, borrowed vanilla/React controls, separate shared/document startup and search-aware persistence retain exact history, failed saves and writer leases. Independent installed mixed table/caption, comment/version and offline-peer workflows pass; a headless Chromium production example checks actual highlight geometry, readonly navigation and one-step Undo. Shared splices preserve original-character provenance. Search highlights now stay visible in fullscreen, including composed fullscreen ancestors, and search tab order is checked on the WebKit host. The installed search browser check runs in the installed-feature-browser candidate profile. The feature remains a candidate: old save keys are not auto-migrated, managed document-only startup does not persist review metadata, and API/performance/platform/release promotion remains open.
features.acceptance: Define literal/Unicode search, navigation and replace-all as one bounded semantic action, excluding hidden or noneditable content by explicit policy.

features.summary: Markdown shortcuts and automatic text transformations
features.current: An explicit Rust policy plans bounded heading/list/quote/task/code/rule and simple inline shortcuts using existing semantic actions and exact history families. Exclusive plain/natural calls retain literal input and isolate conversion Undo. Rule sets are opt-in: markdown-v1, autolink-v1 and typography-v1. They connect through native-capability-checked vanilla/root/React owners, source-bound callback cancellation, ordinary composition/paste/range/remote exclusions and accepted-input refusal reporting. markdown-v1 also converts an existing bullet item to a task, joins a marker typed right after a matching list into that list, and exits a code block on three trailing Enters, each as one isolated Undo step, locally and in shared editors. Independent installed consumers exercise public types, exact reopen and bundle isolation. Pinned earlier local readers restore all 16 native checkpoints and match their Undo/Redo checkpoints, and the installed check verifies the pinned reader artifacts by digest. A repaired whole-source replacement endpoint requires the fixed shared reader; affected older readers reject that case. The input-writing-workflows candidate profile reruns these checks. Physical input methods, hosted CI and final release qualification remain open.
features.acceptance: Add deterministic opt-in rules with composition exclusion, remote-edit boundaries and one-step Undo behavior.

features.summary: Mentions and slash commands
features.current: V4 mention entities (closed kinds user/page/tag, identity = kind + id, label snapshot, `@` marker only) are atomic and inserted by one guarded command in one Undo step, locally and in shared V4 (`insert_mention`, shared `@` menu `mountSharedMentions` / SDK `mountMentions`, atomicity repair under concurrency). Slash commands are one native Undo group locally (`replaceTriggerThen`) and one guarded shared batch, with V4 items for collapsible sections and page breaks. Mention spans import and export identically in local and shared V4 editors. Open: several trigger characters, host-declared kinds or prefixes (`#`) and mention output customization.
features.acceptance: Specify entity identity, async suggestion cancellation, accessible menus and command execution through Rust rather than DOM mutation.

features.summary: Counts, placeholder, fullscreen and outline
features.current: Native Rust counts and a stable-ID outline derive accepted body text; optional Wasm/SDK reads and borrowed vanilla/React controls retain exact save/history families. The contents view tracks the active heading while scrolling and keeps keyboard focus during peer edits. Native placeholder eligibility keeps literal hints outside durable/editable/clipboard content, with admitted startup and live labels. A separately owned browser fullscreen controller borrows the existing local/shared/document coordinator, preserves exact publications and logical selections, keeps remote edits flowing, keeps search and language markers visible, and never adopts/exits a foreign session. Replaceable vanilla/React controls do not close the controller or writer; native cleanup is asynchronous and retryable. Current/pinned-reader workflows, isolated installs and focused headless Chromium production checks exercise these candidates, and the input-writing-workflows and installed-feature-browser candidate profiles rerun them. Physical Escape/input, cross-platform, performance and final V1 qualification remain open.
features.acceptance: Derive counts/outline from admitted AST snapshots, keep placeholders out of content, and preserve focus/selection through fullscreen transitions.

features.summary: Block rearrangement and drop feedback
features.current: File drop and typed block/axis moves exist. Local and shared editors have an opt-in block drag handle with a semantic drop resolver, drop cursor, keyboard pick-up/move and Alt+Shift+Arrow steps, each sending one retained-ID move (shared `move_block` at the planned revision; local native MoveBlock in one exact history group). Missing: inline content drag between positions and a general drop cursor for content drags.
features.acceptance: Move retained IDs rather than copy/delete; add keyboard equivalents and test invalid/cyclic/cross-container targets and shared Undo.

features.summary: Media, details, emoji, math and diagrams
features.current: Rich language V4 adds an original collapsible section (breditor/details with one text-only summary and a flow body, nesting bounded at 8, persisted open state) with wrap/unwrap/open-state commands, deterministic editing, live/static rendering and HTML/Markdown interchange, locally and in shared V4 (`wrap_details`, `unwrap_details`, `set_details_open`, toolbar and slash items, one Undo step each). Shared Enter at a collapsed summary expands it and enters the body in one guarded step like local `enterDetailsBody`, and `<details>` interchange is identical in shared V4. HTML export now preserves significant whitespace in summaries. Missing: HTML embeds, emoji, mathematics, media embeds, audio/video, iframes, diagrams and whiteboards.
features.acceptance: Define original contracts for widgets, HTML embeds and whiteboards. Qualify admission, rendering, recovery, interchange and collaboration for each supported surface.

features.summary: Framework integrations and static rendering
features.current: The private SDK supplies installed local and durable shared vanilla/React entry points. Shared replacement waits for exact old-writer closure; failed save or startup cleanup hands off journal recovery without implicit discard. Tests cover StrictMode, cancellation, rerenders, actual reload, quota failures and database upgrade retention in all three engines. Local-only and shared-without-React installs remain independent. Server rendering of the live editor emits a starting placeholder. A separate inert DOM-free static renderer (@breditor/editor/static) and React BreditorStaticDocument render validated documents with the live link policy, table merge resolution, block layout, presentation styles and exact carriage returns. The static entry is compiled and bundled from clean minimal SDK installs. Docs cover Vue/Svelte/Angular adapter responsibility. Missing: public API/package decisions that make lifecycle hooks stable, remaining source promotion, and non-React framework examples.
features.acceptance: Ship installed-package React and vanilla examples, stable lifecycle hooks and an inert data renderer; document adapter responsibility for other frameworks.

features.summary: Threaded comments and review annotations
features.current: Opt-in native/Wasm/SDK and vanilla/React controls provide durable attributed discussions, mapped/orphaned anchors, resolution, independent comment history, authenticated comment authority and offline transport/recovery. Clean-installed combined review/asset workflows exercise exact reopens and host restart. Host identity/tenant integration and final platform/storage qualification remain release gates, not comments API claims.
features.acceptance: Design durable mapped anchors, thread permissions, resolution/orphan policy, offline merging and independent comment history before building UI.

features.summary: Suggestions and tracked changes
features.current: Source-bound attributed text, formatting, list, table and image proposals leave accepted content unchanged until an authenticated once-only server decision. Offline decision queues, owned accepted-effect Undo/Redo, manual revisions and bounded automatic formatting/text rebasing reach installed vanilla/React controls. Native suggestion and revision delivery run as candidate qualification jobs on the current runtime. Accepted document export remains separate from proposal/review metadata and outboxes. Missing: review-aware export, production permissions, automatic rebase for mixed commands, external change-set review and release promotion.
features.acceptance: Define suggestions for text, formatting, lists, tables and images with attribution, permissions, concurrent accept/reject and explicit export semantics.

features.summary: Named versions, comparison and restore
features.current: Immutable named versions retain source proofs, semantic comparison and explicit guarded restore as a fresh edit. An authenticated shared catalog, optional SDK cache and borrowed vanilla/React controls preserve independent document/review journals and fresh writer identity. Clean-installed combined workflows cover stale/conflicting restore, exact recovery, offline edits and host restart. The reference host's version HTTP path holds each request's permission check, body, native work and buffered response inside four per-room slots and answers HTTP 503 at capacity. Missing: automatic snapshots on change (automatic-version-snapshots-on-change@1). Asset retention, bounded catalog/journal lifetime and final production qualification remain open release gates.
features.acceptance: Separate user-facing document versions from runtime journals and GC; restore without reusing old writer identity or overwriting concurrent work.

features.summary: Word, XML, PDF and other document conversion
features.current: A dependency-free deterministic DOCX exporter (@breditor/interchange/docx, STORE-only zip, fixed timestamps) maps headings, inline formats, links, hard line breaks, lists incl. V4 numbering and descending decimal markers, quotes, code, rules, page breaks, tables with merges and captions, host-supplied images and bookmarks, reporting every unrepresentable feature as a loss. Page options are validated before host images load, and transferred or reused image buffers are reported or copied. A clean install of the DOCX-only entry and bundle is qualified. The XML v1 exporter (@breditor/interchange/xml) serializes the native clipboard projection with ordered nodes, typed properties, asset bindings and source-bound native document identity. Installed local and shared SDK checks parse exact XML from restored checkpoints. Missing: DOCX import, PDF, ODT, EPUB and legacy .doc export, and verified opening in Word or LibreOffice (LibreOffice and Word rendering have not been run).
features.acceptance: Qualify self-hostable conversion adapters, including a versioned XML export. Set fidelity targets, preserve document and asset bindings and report unsupported content.

features.summary: Pages, page breaks and print layout
features.current: The editor stores canonical flow (docs/PAGINATION_AND_PRINT.md). Rich language V4 has an explicit root-level page-break block (insert/delete, node selection, navigation stop, clipboard, Word/Docs/CSS page-break import), locally and in shared V4, with identical import in both. An opt-in print layer sets A4/Letter, orientation, margins and break avoidance, repeats header rows in static print output, and adds an optional one-line running header and a current/total page-number footer through page-margin boxes. A mounted screen preview works inside shadow roots, keeps concurrent previews separate and measures content height and numbered page starts, honoring page-break markers. A macOS check (scripts/check-measured-print-output.mjs) compares Chromium PDF output for a fixed-font fixture with the measured preview page count and forced page, and checks the running header and page counters with PDFKit. Missing: a dated qualification record of that check, Firefox and WebKit printed output, documented tolerances, header-row repetition when printing the live editor, a paged editing view with zoom and page navigation, and header/footer content or number fields stored in the document.
features.acceptance: Qualify measured pagination, page numbers and running headers against physical browser output, with pinned fonts and settings and documented tolerances.

features.summary: Templates, merge fields, footnotes and bookmarks
features.current: Rich language V4 adds unique named bookmarks on text blocks and `#name` internal links, locally and in shared V4 (`set_bookmark`, `rename_bookmark` retargeting every link in one group, document-order uniqueness repair, bookmark index): dangling links are allowed but reported, and HTML anchors, Markdown fallback and DOCX bookmarks interchange identically in local and shared V4. Bookmarks attach to blocks, not arbitrary inline positions (CKEditor places inline anchors; inline-bookmark-position@1 stays V1 work), and cut drops them. Footnotes/endnotes, templates, merge fields, template slots/variables and cross-reference fields are missing.
features.acceptance: Design reference integrity, field/value trust, permissions and shared history; define behavior when referenced content is moved or removed.

features.summary: AI assistance and integrated spelling or grammar review
features.current: An opt-in provider-agnostic contract exists for local and shared editors: hosts supply rewrite and language-check providers, only explicitly scoped plain text is sent with cancellation, deadlines and size bounds, provider output is validated as untrusted, rewrites are reviewed and applied as one guarded command with stale refusal (in shared editors, one guarded native plain-text range replacement that stales only when its target region changes), and language issues are painted outside the editing DOM, including in fullscreen. An opt-in agent tool contract adds schema-validated, revision-bound, reviewable agent edits (see ai-agents-and-server-api). Missing: formatted-scope requests, bundled or qualified providers (including a WProofreader-style language review provider), AI chat, quick actions, custom prompts, translation UI and inline completion, all of which are V1 catalog cases.
features.acceptance: Define explicit host providers and privacy boundaries; generated edits must use ordinary guarded commands with stale-result rejection and reviewable history.

features.summary: Source editing, general HTML and email layouts
features.current: The schema-bound profile round-trips semantic body fragments. `exportHtmlPage` wraps the admitted body in a complete page with bounded host title, description, language and direction, and `importHtmlPage` returns the native body plus editable host metadata, dropping external stylesheets, base/refresh directives and other head content with a notice. HTML import inlines bounded ancestor-scoped and direct-child stylesheet rules and honors authored alignment in legacy email center wrappers. An opt-in document-selection source view edits sanitized semantic HTML in a textarea, previews bounded allowlist losses before any change, keeps drafts and authored final paragraphs, and applies one guarded whole-document paste. Missing: General HTML Support for elements and attributes outside the schema, HTML comments, HTML embeds, email layout tables and presets, stylesheet-to-inline-style export, and a source view for shared and ordinary editors.
features.acceptance: Qualify general HTML support, full-page round trips, email layouts and inline-style export. Define policy-controlled admission, preview, restore and export for untrusted markup.

features.summary: Multiple editable roots in one document
features.current: Local rich editors support multiple editable roots as a root set of ordinary V1–V4 documents with no grammar change (docs/MULTIPLE_ROOTS.md): stable root ids, labels, attributes and order; one active root (cross-root selections are not expressible by design, as in CKEditor); and one native history owner that keeps a single global Undo/Redo order across roots and routes Undo/Redo to the owning root. `mountRichMultiRootEditor` mounts one surface per root with one shared toolbar that follows focus, with per-root data, add/remove root and a versioned `breditor/rich-root-set` checkpoint that re-verifies every root's history. Missing: undoable add/remove root and root attributes, shared real-time multi-root (specified: one room per root, a client journal and a replicated set manifest) and whole-set interchange.
features.acceptance: Specify root identity, cross-root selections, shared ordering and one history owner before advertising multi-root parity.

features.summary: Localized UI, bidirectional content and language metadata
features.current: Unicode text is retained. An opt-in validated UI catalog localizes local and shared chrome, toolbars, context UI, slash, resize and drag handles, scrollable-table labels, the search, writing, fullscreen, review and suggestion panels, clipboard status lines and code-keyed user refusals, with chrome-only lang/dir; default English output is byte-identical and only English ships. Rich language V4 adds canonical BCP 47 text-run language (`lang`), locally and in shared V4 (`setTextLanguage`, Language control), with identical `lang`/`xml:lang` interchange. Missing: inline `dir` on language runs (text-part-language-and-direction@1 keeps this in V1 scope), shipped translations, localized native error strings and qualified mixed-direction (RTL/bidi) editing.
features.acceptance: Separate UI language from content direction, localize control strings and qualify mixed-direction navigation/selection with language metadata.

features.summary: Skip-level lists, multi-block list items and legal multi-level numbering
features.current: Rich V1–V4 already admit multi-block list items (a leading paragraph or heading followed by any flow, including paragraphs after a child list). Native JoinListItems/SplitListItem block captures (exact inverses, one Undo step each) back local `joinListItems` `blocks` / `splitListItemBlock` and shared `join_list_items` `blocks` / `split_list_item_block`, with CKEditor-style keys in local and shared editors: Backspace in an empty item head keeps it as a later block of the previous item, Enter in an empty later block splits it out, and Tab/Shift+Tab indent and outdent from any block. HTML, Markdown and DOCX handling of multi-block items is tested. Legal multi-level numbering is an opt-in, presentation-only `legalListNumbering` option. Missing: skip-level items and stored legal numbering, both needing a grammar change (specified as a V5 candidate in docs/LIST_STRUCTURE.md), task-item multi-block keys, and keyboard/screen-reader qualification.
features.acceptance: Specify multi-block items, skip-level structure and legal counters through native list actions, history, shared replay and interchange, or record each as an approved exclusion.

features.summary: Syntax-highlighted code blocks
features.current: An opt-in local and shared SDK decorator derives bounded CSS highlight ranges from explicit JavaScript, TypeScript, JSON, Python and Rust labels. Static HTML can use the same tokenizer and palette to publish escaped syntax-colored code. Editor DOM, selection offsets and serialized content are unchanged. Unsupported languages, oversized blocks and browsers without the CSS Custom Highlight API display plain code; the bounds and fallback are documented in docs/RICH_STRUCTURAL_V2.md. Chromium, Firefox and WebKit specs cover local and shared editors. No exact release candidate has been tagged.
features.acceptance: Qualify the bounded language set and styling on the supported browser matrix and exact release candidate. Record supported languages and plain-code fallback in integration docs.

features.summary: Typographic replacements and autocorrect
features.current: Opt-in native `typography-v1` input-rule set (`inputRules: "typography-v1"` or `{rule, include, exclude, quotes}`): smart quotes with apostrophes and locale presets (English, German, French with no-break spaces, Swiss, Polish) or a validated custom pair; ellipsis, delimited en/em dashes, (c)/(r)/(tm), delimited fractions and arrows, <=/>=/!= and an opt-in misc group. Rules are chosen by CKEditor-style groups and names, validated natively and at mount. Each replacement is one native Undo group that restores exactly the typed characters and keeps their formats; nothing converts in code, on paste, during IME composition, on remote updates or when read-only. Local and shared editors behave identically. Exact checkpoints from the two pinned earlier local readers are re-verified against the current runtime. Not supported: host-configured custom replacement rules (CKEditor `extra`, catalog case configured-text-replacement-rules@1), Tiptap per-rule output overrides and RTL swap, and undelimited `--`, `->` and `2x3` forms.
features.acceptance: Add opt-in, locale-aware replacements as native input rules with one-step Undo of the replacement, composition safety and shared parity.

features.summary: Special characters, case change, format painter and named styles
features.current: Opt-in special characters, case change and format painter for local and shared rich editors (docs/FORMATTING_PRODUCTIVITY.md). The picker has five built-in categories, validated host categories, name and code-point search, an accessible keyboard grid and localized names, inserting through native text input in one Undo step. Case change is a native Rust command (local `changeSelectionCase`, shared guarded `ReplaceTextRange` splices): UPPER, lower, Title Case with configurable minor words and Shift+F3 cycling, full Unicode mapping (ß→SS, final sigma, titlecase digraphs; Turkic i only for an explicit tr/az locale), preserving format runs, identities and mentions in one Undo step that converges across peers. The format painter copies inline text formatting (single-use, double-click sticky, Escape cancels) and applies it as one selection-format change. Missing: named styles and highlight presets. The doc calls them an intentional difference, but no approval is recorded and named-formatting-presets@1 is in V1 scope.
features.acceptance: Specify each tool through existing typed format commands (one Undo step, local and shared) or record named styles as an approved difference.

features.summary: In-document table of contents
features.current: The local and shared editor contents presentation nests native heading reads, navigates with revision-guarded selection, keeps keyboard focus during peer edits and marks the current section as the viewport or host scroll container moves. Static HTML can prepend a linked contents list using stable heading IDs and existing bookmark anchors, with whitespace-trimmed labels. Placement is host-controlled. Missing: a movable, saved contents block in the document (movable-persisted-table-of-contents@1) and contents in non-HTML output such as DOCX.
features.acceptance: Define or explicitly scope the movable, saved contents block and non-HTML export behavior. Qualify the selected workflow on exact release artifacts.

features.summary: Show blocks, invisible characters, minimap, document title and focus styling
features.current: Opt-in show-blocks, invisible-character and focused-block aids (`mountRichEditingAids`; SDK `mountEditingAids`) work in local and shared editors (docs/EDITING_AIDS.md). Show blocks outlines every rendered block and labels its type from the UI catalog; invisible characters marks spaces, no-break spaces, tabs, hard breaks and paragraph ends, with a bounded scan per frame; an optional attribute follows the caret's block. Everything is painted in an aria-hidden, pointer-transparent layer outside the editable DOM, and toggling (buttons or Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+Shift+B/P) is never a command, publication or Undo step and leaves caret movement, typing, Copy and static output unchanged, checked in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. Missing: a content minimap and a separate document-title field (both V1 catalog cases; a title needs document structure the frozen V4 grammar does not have).
features.acceptance: Add each aid as an inert presentation layer that never enters the document model, with accessibility checks.

features.summary: Ruby (furigana) annotations
features.current: Ruby is an opt-in first-party typed inline extension, `breditor-ruby/ruby`, with one required 1–256 byte annotation and no grammar change; profiles that include it get their own fingerprint while V1–V4 stay frozen (docs/RUBY_ANNOTATIONS.md). Local and shared Ruby and Remove ruby controls set, replace or remove a validated reading on a selection or the caret's group, each as one Undo step through the generic typed-format commands, with exact replay and shared convergence; typing never inherits a reading. Live and static output render `<ruby>base<rp>(</rp><rt>…</rt><rp>)</rp></ruby>` with the live reading as non-editable generated content. HTML import/export maps `<ruby>` for ruby-capable local and shared owners, Markdown falls back to exact HTML and DOCX writes `w:ruby`. Not supported: nested or double-sided ruby and position options.
features.acceptance: Specify ruby as a typed inline structure with base/annotation text, selection, history, rendering and interchange, or record an approved exclusion.

features.summary: Autosave contract for rich and shared sessions
features.current: Base-text sessions have checkpoint autosave and shared sessions persist durably. The local rich SDK offers opt-in debounced checkpoint autosave (`@breditor/editor/autosave`) for a host-owned single-writer storage key, with ordered writes, status, flush and explicit retry. A source-build browser test covers coalesced saves, exact history after reload and a failed write that stays dirty until retry; a clean minimal SDK install saves exact local history in Node; the rich demo shows autosave and retry. Missing: qualification on the exact supported browser artifacts (installed packages in each supported browser), busy editor lifetimes and the writer-ownership transfer in autosave-failure-retry-and-writer-ownership@1. Hosts own cross-tab exclusivity.
features.acceptance: Qualify the opt-in rich local workflow on the exact supported browser artifacts, including stored-session reload, busy editor lifetimes and write failures. Hosts own cross-tab exclusivity.

features.summary: Menu bar, editor layouts and keyboard help dialog
features.current: Opt-in editor shell for local, shared and SDK rich editors (docs/EDITOR_SHELL.md): a WAI-ARIA menu bar (Alt+F9, arrows, typeahead, Escape back to the text; configurable menus checked at mount) and an empty-line block menu (Alt+F10; never takes focus) borrow admitted toolbar controls, so items show the same Rust-derived state and run one command and one Undo step. Tab and Shift+Tab inside an open field form now follow the form's native order instead of closing the menu. An Alt+0 modal help dialog (focus trap, platform-aware keys, localized) lists a read-only shortcut registry built from the editors' own chords and mounted add-ons, and a balloon-block preset composes the selection toolbar, block menu and help. Covered by jsdom contracts, rich-browser specs in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit and a two-writer shared spec. Missing: real screen-reader qualification, right-to-left chrome checks, external toolbar mounting and the WCAG 2.2 review.
features.acceptance: Add a menu bar and shortcut help dialog built from admitted controls and the shortcut registry, with keyboard and screen-reader qualification.

features.summary: AI agents, document server API and webhooks
features.current: An opt-in, provider-agnostic agent tool contract (docs/AI_AGENT_TOOLS.md) gives a host's LLM nine typed tools with closed JSON Schemas to read the document in chunks, find text, read the selection and edit by block id and offset. Every call is validated as untrusted input against the schema, the document and the native grammar, bounded, bound to the revision the agent read and re-based only when every target is unchanged. Edits are reviewable by default: a staged change set accepted as one native publication and Undo step (native `commandGroup` locally, one guarded shared dispatch in rooms) or suggestion proposals; direct mode is opt-in; a review panel and an MCP-shaped adapter are included with no bundled model or network code. The reference relay adds an opt-in authenticated document server (docs/DOCUMENT_SERVER_API.md): room listing, canonical JSON snapshots with an exact revision, room creation, owner-only archive, comment threads, server-side injection of allowlisted native shared commands at an exact base revision as a service writer (one history group that clients see as a normal remote change), and HMAC-signed webhooks with retries and a delivery log. Request bodies are bounded before they are read. Missing: AI chat and translate UI, relay-backed agent proposals, identity-provider auth, version and bulk endpoints, Rust HTML/Markdown export, durable webhook queues and outbound TLS (public-relay gate).
features.acceptance: Define a bounded, authenticated tool and server API over the native core (read, propose as suggestions, apply) with audit and authority checks before claiming parity.

features.summary: Content Security Policy guidance and crash restart
features.current: Journal recovery and exact reload exist, and a synchronously failed SDK runtime import can be retried. There is no documented strict CSP or Trusted Types policy for the editor and its Wasm runtime, no test under such a policy, and no opt-in watchdog that restarts a crashed editor from a verified durable checkpoint.
features.acceptance: Document and test a strict CSP (including Wasm requirements) and an opt-in crash-restart path that restores from durable state.

gates.current: Still holds on main. The checker reports all 57 feature groups with acceptance cases (241 cases), and Tiptap (93/93) and CKEditor 5 (160/160) entries are mapped with none unmapped. docs/V1_CATALOG_BASELINE.md records zero approved exclusions or deviations.
gates.acceptance: Expand the Tiptap 3.35 and CKEditor 5 v49.1 catalog rows into versioned acceptance cases. The reviewed capabilities in docs/V1_RELEASE_PLAN.md are all in V1 scope, including the capabilities previously proposed for exclusion. Track coverage per capability and document approved intentional differences.

gates.summary: Promote rich/shared Rust, Wasm and browser packages
gates.current: Still holds on main. Every package is at 0.3.0-alpha.22, which matches docs/INTEGRATE_EDITOR.md and the 2026-11-22 archive record. The package build and check scripts named as evidence are present. New subpath exports (xml, portable-html) and an optional peer were added without new third-party dependencies. The RC must recheck the clean install against the final archives.
gates.acceptance: A clean consumer installs one supported paired profile and production module; no experiments path, manual target artifact or source-only link is required.

gates.summary: Freeze V1 APIs and explicit migration contracts
gates.current: COMPATIBILITY.md now documents source API, Wasm ABI, schema, history/journal and raster-asset compatibility separately. Frozen historical fixtures restore byte-exact with deliberate refusals for: the V0.1.0 (ABI 2) checkpoint, the V0.2.1 Highlight (ABI 3) checkpoint, the alpha.6 ABI 4 typed-range checkpoint, pre-V4 rich language 1-3 checkpoints (native and installed readers), the first shared structural V2 and first shared layout (V3) SDK journals, and the first Raster Archive V1 producer bytes. The pinned local input-rule readers are qualified, and an installed source API inventory exists for review. Remaining: an approved V1 API surface and change policy, shared input-rule reader and browser routing evidence, and shared upgrade and rollback routes.
gates.acceptance: Document source, ABI, schema, journal and asset compatibility separately; add supported old-version recovery/migration fixtures and deliberate rejection paths.

gates.summary: Cover every distributed feature in the release pipeline
gates.current: The manual candidate workflow now has focused profiles and shards for the default, editor, rich and shared browser matrices, relay recovery, installed distribution, installed application network and input workflows. It retains failed-stage Playwright reports and runner context, binds stage evidence to the candidate plan, and can authenticate hosted artifacts and combine cumulative coverage. A PR readiness workflow runs ledger and runner contract tests on pull requests. Remaining: no retained record shows a successful hosted run, or combined authenticated coverage with --require-complete, covering every engineering stage for one exact candidate. The candidate workflow is manual-dispatch only.
gates.acceptance: Default verify:release alone is insufficient. Run default, rich, shared, relay and installed-consumer checks reproducibly in CI, retaining exact candidate hashes and failed runs.

gates.summary: Qualify browser faults and native clipboard
gates.current: Overlapping default Wasm startup now keeps the first live instance in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. Exact unsigned round trips for descriptor string bounds address the reproduced WebKit descriptor rejection, and the stress oracle passed 20 x 10,000 restores. Native Safari (manual paste, Undo/Redo, save and reload, keyboard typing history) and installed Chrome (repeated lifecycle and trusted clipboard rounds) have dated records. A repeated installed network lifecycle runner exists. Remaining: the intermittent WebKit initial-projection rejection and the original editing faults have no cause or repair and no supported-environment policy. Safari has only single manual sessions, with no repeated lifecycle or clipboard runs, and the exact RC has no integrated browser qualification.
gates.acceptance: Close or explicitly resolve the historical WebKit fault with a reproducible cause/fix or supported-environment policy, and qualify native Safari/Chrome plus repeated lifecycle/clipboard sessions. Passing isolated files is not an engine repair.

gates.summary: Qualify keyboard, accessibility semantics and touch layout
gates.current: A manual native Safari 26.6.2 pass on installed alpha.22 archives covered keyboard-only focus order, the browser accessibility tree, system-pasteboard paste and Undo/Redo across a save and reload. Automated specs cover editor menu form tab order and pilot narrow-width, 44 px touch-target and recovery-focus behaviour. Real IME, VoiceOver or other screen-reader speech, and physical mobile/touch devices remain untested, and nothing ran on the final integrated artifact. Real-person screen-reader, physical IME and device testing is no longer required for V1.
gates.acceptance: On the final integrated artifact, pass automated keyboard-only, accessibility-tree/ARIA, IME composition-event and emulated mobile/touch-layout checks. Testing by outside people with real screen readers, physical IMEs or mobile devices is outside V1 scope (approved 2026-11-27).

gates.summary: Approve measured latency, memory and download budgets
gates.current: Installed-fixture measurements now exist for typing, paste and Undo latency, shared history latency, reconnect, startup, shared and closed paired-session memory, raster asset reads and writes, and native relay cold start. All were taken on one Apple M1 Pro host, mostly in Chrome 157/158, and the default size budgets were not raised. Supported document, table, image, history and peer sizes are not set, no process memory budget or long-session memory result exists, and latency was not measured on other named hardware.
gates.acceptance: Set supported document/table/image/history/peer sizes and measure startup, typing, paste, Undo, reconnect and long-session memory on named hardware/browser versions. Do not silently raise existing default budgets.

gates.current: HTTP raster uploads are now bounded, and an opt-in loopback mode (`serve ... --isolated-raster`) checks each upload in a supervised one-shot subprocess with a 15-second deadline and Unix rlimits. The host reports admission outcome counters and drains transfers on shutdown, and a SIGKILL restart is qualified. Still missing: TLS, an identity provider and tenant integration (the CLI refuses non-loopback binds), host-wide quotas and abuse limits, filesystem/network containment, isolation for the other native import/decode paths, and deployment tests.
gates.acceptance: Provide import/decode work isolation, TLS/identity/tenant integration, abuse limits, observability and deployment tests. Loopback demo tokens and best-effort decoder limits are not public production isolation.

gates.summary: Handle history limits, backup and compaction
gates.current: Installed Chrome records show the explicit generation family keeping pre-cut Undo/Redo and an offline edit across rollover and across two seals per writer. Without rollover, the original shared journal hits its 16 MiB budget in round 109 of the boundary workload. Relay storage costs and cold-start replay memory are also measured. Still missing: a defined supported document lifetime, automatic generation selection, physical server-log rotation, asset garbage collection and retention policy, negotiated client/server retention, coordinated restore drills on the RC.
gates.acceptance: Preserve Undo/Redo and outstanding offline edits across generations, as approved by the user; a history-resetting rollover does not satisfy V1. Define document lifetime at current journal/log/asset bounds, safe compaction and asset retention, and coordinated restore drills. Independent-writer credential recovery is outside V1 scope (approved 2026-11-27).

gates.summary: Audit the actual V1 dependency and license graph
gates.current: Mostly holds on main. The rich and shared Wasm Cargo.lock hashes still match the 2026-11-23 review. The native relay lock does not: a98c569f (Nov 24) added rlimit 0.11.0 to the relay server graph, so the lock moved from 21f274c5 to 6572cd47 and the recorded relay inventory is one crate stale. Re-run build-relay-notices and record the updated relay inventory before or at the RC recheck.
gates.acceptance: Generate and review notices/SBOM for browser, Wasm and native relay artifacts, including the pinned replication patch and decoders; verify reproducibility and vulnerability response ownership.

gates.summary: Ship coherent SDK documentation and support policy
gates.current: Still holds on main. README.md, docs/INTEGRATE_EDITOR.md, docs/COMPATIBILITY.md, SECURITY.md and CONTRIBUTING.md are present and name the same 0.3.0-alpha.22 archives as the packages. Since the review they gained historical-reader qualification notes. The RC must recheck the docs against the final archives.
gates.acceptance: Publish one install/quickstart, capability/support matrix, host asset/auth responsibilities, security reporting, troubleshooting, upgrade guide and contribution policy that match the actual archives.

gates.current: Tooling for the RC exists: check-v1-readiness.mjs --require-pre-rc checks that only this gate remains, and check-candidate-coverage.mjs validates complete candidate stage evidence. The ledger still has open prerequisite gates and feature gaps. No RC tag exists after v0.3.0-alpha.22, so clean installs, immutable-hash gate verification and publication/deployment approval have not happened.
gates.acceptance: After all required scope and qualification work, tag a reviewed RC, verify clean installs and every gate against immutable hashes, then obtain separate publication/deployment approval.
